records.name: Agente
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 1. Agente

**Relevant niches:** Education; Ecommerce.  
**Project evidence:** WorkFusion Automation Academy; Atterley.  
**Source records:** E25, E26.

**Why include:** Adds concrete learning-platform and commerce experience. The portfolio identifies UX/UI work for Automation Academy, while Atterley's case describes information architecture, catalog/product pages and checkout redesign.

**Limits and questions:** Some work is historical. Confirm recent delivery staff and the exact scope proposed. Do not assign Real Estate from a PropTech service-page claim alone.

records.name: Arounda
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 2. Arounda

**Relevant niches:** Fintech.  
**Project evidence:** PIIFUND.  
**Source records:** E27.

**Why include:** A useful fintech-focused addition. Its PIIFUND case describes banking, microloan and insurance flows, including onboarding and use on weak connections. The account identifies UX, wireframes and UI work rather than a logo-only relationship.

**Limits and questions:** Deployment and compliance are agency-reported. Request current comparable financial-product work; do not extend this case into unrelated niches.

records.name: Aufait UX
records.evidence_summary: DAMAC Agents; iD Fresh; Parul University; E28/E29/E30
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 3. Aufait UX

**Relevant niches:** Real Estate; Logistics; Education.  
**Project evidence:** DAMAC Agents; iD Fresh; Parul University.  
**Source records:** E28, E29, E30.

**Why include:** Helps cover three otherwise thinner areas. DAMAC documents broker-facing property search and booking; iD Fresh documents field research and distribution workflows; Parul documents information architecture for a large university website.

**Limits and questions:** Label Parul as an institutional website, not an LMS. DAMAC supports an agent workflow, not every tenant or property-transaction use case.

records.name: Cieden
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 4. Cieden

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** Clinicmaster.  
**Source records:** E31.

**Why include:** Relevant for complex clinical and practice-management software. The Clinicmaster account describes modernization across patient records, billing and charting, with workflow and design-system considerations.

**Limits and questions:** The source describes a validated direction ready for continued rollout. Do not call it an independently audited platform-wide deployment or compliance certification. Sitenna alone is not Logistics/Real Estate proof.

records.name: CorLab Tech
records.evidence_summary: Data visualization and Logistics service pages; E55/E56
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 5. CorLab Tech

**Relevant niches:** Logistics, by explicit owner selection.  
**Evidence:** Data visualization services; Logistics service page.  
**Source records:** E55, E56.  
**Evidence depth:** Service-level; no named logistics client case established by these pages.

**Why include:** Adds a development-oriented candidate for operational dashboards and maps. Its Logistics page describes transport, warehouse and delivery software services. The owner selected position #5; that position is not a measured comparison of client outcomes.

**Limits and questions:** Confirm the proposed UX research/design team, a comparable named logistics engagement and shipped contribution. Public service descriptions do not establish project delivery, usability testing or achieved results. Keep the service-level label on the profile and Logistics list. Do not add Healthcare or AI & ML memberships from service claims alone.

records.name: Fantasy
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 6. Fantasy

**Relevant niches:** AI & ML; Fintech.  
**Project evidence:** BNY Eliza.  
**Source records:** E32.

**Why include:** Brings enterprise AI and bank-employee workflow evidence. Fantasy describes vision/interface work and a coded design-system contribution for BNY Eliza. This supports internal financial-services AI rather than just an AI-company website.

**Limits and questions:** Credit the vision and design-system scope. Do not attribute the entire platform, model, bank adoption or reported operational results to Fantasy.

records.name: Fuselab Creative
records.evidence_summary: ClyHealth; DHCS; Stardog Voicebox; Robodog AGV; Hyperfab; E05/E06/E07/E22/E23
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 7. Fuselab Creative

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare; Robotics; AI & ML; Logistics.  
**Project evidence:** ClyHealth; DHCS; Stardog Voicebox; Robodog AGV; Hyperfab.  
**Source records:** E05, E06, E07, E22, E23.

**Why include:** Useful for data-rich clinical/administrative products, conversational data tools and robotics interfaces. Several sources support distinct contexts, including warehouse fleet/mission controls; that warehouse context can also support a narrowly described Logistics placement.

**Limits and questions:** Separate provider-facing work from public-health reporting, industrial robotics from warehouse operations, and design from hardware engineering. Deployment, safety and clinical outcomes are not independently verified. Disclose any material publisher relationship.

records.name: Fuzzy Math
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 8. Fuzzy Math

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** GE Healthcare.  
**Source records:** E08.

**Why include:** Adds enterprise healthcare research and reusable interaction-pattern experience. The source describes work across clinical, imaging and administrative products, including data interpretation and legacy-system consistency.

**Limits and questions:** The account covers R&D and product exploration. It does not establish that every illustrated concept shipped, and should not be marketed as generic medical-device certification.

records.name: GoInvo
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 9. GoInvo

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare; AI & ML.  
**Project evidence:** Maya EHR; Ipsos Facto.  
**Source records:** E09, E10.

**Why include:** Strong candidate for healthcare systems and research-centered AI. Maya provides concrete home-health workflow evidence; Facto describes guided AI research, contextual tools and source transparency.

**Limits and questions:** Maya's working-product status is agency-reported. Facto mixes shipped improvements with prototypes for future work; preserve that distinction and omit unaudited usage claims.

records.name: Guidea
records.evidence_summary: Amalgam Rx; Humana population-health platform; Express Scripts; E33
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 10. Guidea

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** Amalgam Rx; Humana population-health platform; Express Scripts.  
**Source records:** E33.

**Why include:** An industry-focused healthcare inclusion. Its public portfolio names platform-design and population-health contexts, giving the list a specialist beyond general product studios.

**Limits and questions:** This source is a portfolio overview with uneven project detail. Add a stronger project walkthrough or reference before using high-confidence process/outcome claims. Do not turn partner product clearances into agency-wide certification.

records.name: HTEC Momentum
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 11. HTEC Momentum

**Relevant niches:** Logistics; Fintech; AI & ML.  
**Project evidence:** Sifted; Bitstamp.  
**Source records:** E34, E35.

**Why include:** Sifted supplies specific supply-chain and ML-recommendation experience, including reorganizing how shippers find actionable insight. Bitstamp supplies product-strategy and mobile trading-app design evidence.

**Limits and questions:** Use the current HTEC Momentum display name and retain Momentum Design Lab as an alias. Do not treat HTEC's company-wide services or headcount as the actual proposed design team, or publish unaudited results.

records.name: Lazarev.agency
records.membership_note: Healthcare (wellness); Fintech; Ecommerce; Real Estate; AI & ML
records.evidence_summary: Accern Rhea; WellSet; Matta; CoHome; E12/E51/E52/E53
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 12. Lazarev.agency

**Relevant niches:** AI & ML; Fintech; Ecommerce; Real Estate; Healthcare (qualified wellness).  
**Project evidence:** Accern Rhea; Matta; CoHome; WellSet.  
**Source records:** E12, E51, E52, E53.

**Why include:** Rhea supports AI-assisted financial research. Additional named cases establish B2B chemical purchasing in Matta, property/co-ownership acquisition UX in CoHome, and wellness discovery, scheduling and personalization in WellSet.

**Limits and questions:** WellSet does not establish clinical/EHR expertise. Matta is industrial commerce. CoHome supports its documented property-exploration and website/funnel scope. Funding, acquisition, clinical outcomes and regulatory validation are not inferred.

records.name: Metalab
records.evidence_summary: Midjourney; Suno; robotics virtual-testing portfolio item; E13
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 13. Metalab

**Relevant niches:** AI & ML; Robotics.  
**Project evidence:** Midjourney; Suno; robotics virtual-testing portfolio item.  
**Source records:** E13.

**Why include:** Adds actual AI product examples, with selected portfolio items identifying product design and implementation contributions. A robotics-testing infrastructure entry also supports a limited simulation/developer-tools placement.

**Limits and questions:** The Robotics placement is qualified and portfolio-level, not physical robot-control evidence. The source mixes product, branding and website work; qualify each item separately and seek deeper detail before a high robotics rank.

records.name: Netguru
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 14. Netguru

**Relevant niches:** Real Estate; Education; Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** Otodom; UCLA Chorus; Aspit.  
**Source records:** E36, E37, E54.

**Why include:** Otodom describes embedded property-marketplace research/design/testing; Chorus supplies academic app-creation UX; Aspit identifies healthcare product design and engineering work for medical-professional software.

**Limits and questions:** Credit the actual design contribution within its combined design/engineering model. Academic tooling is not generic LMS proof. Aspit's public process description is less detailed than the leading specialist healthcare cases.

records.name: Neuron
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 15. Neuron

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** iQuartic.  
**Source records:** E15.

**Why include:** Relevant for health-insurance administration and medical-coding tools. The case identifies workflow research with subject-matter experts, interface modernization and a React frontend contribution.

**Limits and questions:** Insurance risk adjustment and coding are distinct from treatment decisions or bedside clinical software. Keep the recommendation within that operational context.

records.name: Qubstudio
records.membership_note: Healthcare; Fintech; Ecommerce; Logistics; Education; AI & ML
records.evidence_summary: Ademrius; Gulf Bank/ila Bank; BluePallet; MyTower; LinkIt!; Wade & Wendy; E16/E17/E38/E39/E40
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 16. Qubstudio

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare; Fintech; Ecommerce; Logistics; Education; AI & ML.  
**Project evidence:** Ademrius; Gulf Bank/ila Bank; BluePallet; MyTower; LinkIt!; Wade & Wendy.  
**Source records:** E16, E17, E38, E39, E40.

**Why include:** A useful coverage anchor with different named evidence for different niches. LinkIt! supports student/parent/staff product work; BluePallet supports industrial commerce; MyTower supports transportation-management IA/UX. The client portfolio also identifies banking work.

**Limits and questions:** Use the relevant project per list. MyTower/banking entries have less public depth than full cases; historical recruitment AI is not generic modern-agent expertise. Do not import infrastructure branding work as PropTech product evidence.

records.name: Think Company
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 17. Think Company

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare.  
**Project evidence:** Nemours Children's Health.  
**Source records:** E19.

**Why include:** Adds healthcare research and family-provider experience. The source describes interviews, a telemedicine pilot and later product evolution with the care organization.

**Limits and questions:** Its workforce analytics work is not another primary niche in this eight-category plan. Attribute healthcare outcomes and separate agency contribution from the whole health-system product.

records.name: ustwo
records.membership_note: Healthcare; Fintech; Ecommerce; Logistics; Education; Robotics; AI & ML
records.evidence_summary: Fresenius; Brilliant.org; Inflection Pi; Alphabet; SharkClean; EPI; Lush; E41/E42/E43/E44/E45/E46/E47
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 18. ustwo

**Relevant niches:** Healthcare; Fintech; Ecommerce; Logistics; Education; Robotics; AI & ML.  
**Project evidence:** Fresenius; Brilliant.org; Inflection Pi; Alphabet; SharkClean; EPI; Lush.  
**Source records:** E41, E42, E43, E44, E45, E46, E47.

**Why include:** The broadest documented coverage in this research set, with separate cases rather than one generic claim. Fresenius covers clinician/patient experiences; Brilliant covers learning engagement; Pi covers AI interaction; SharkClean covers consumer robot controls. Other cases support payments, fleet-driver tools and mobile commerce.

**Limits and questions:** Breadth is not a quality score. EPI includes vision/prototype foundations; Brilliant includes a tested North Star concept; Lush is historical. Alphabet is BMW Group's mobility business, not Google's parent; its driver app is not freight dispatch. Consumer robotics is distinct from industrial fleet control.

records.name: UXDA
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 19. UXDA

**Relevant niches:** Fintech.  
**Project evidence:** United Arab Bank.  
**Source records:** E48.

**Why include:** An explicit financial-UX specialist. The UAB case describes redesigning customer banking tasks and mobile flows rather than a general corporate brand website.

**Limits and questions:** Do not distribute it across unrelated sectors from reputation alone. Confirm the current team and relevant retail/corporate banking scope; published metrics remain agency-reported.

records.name: UX Studio
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 20. UX Studio

**Relevant niches:** AI & ML; Robotics; Education.  
**Project evidence:** OverseeAI; Revolution Robotics.  
**Source records:** E21, E24.

**Why include:** Adds a research-led AI-monitoring example and a distinct educational robotics example. Revolution describes configuration, coding and control, with research and testing involving children.

**Limits and questions:** OverseeAI is POC/MVP evidence. Revolution's Education and Robotics placements share one case and do not establish industrial control expertise or broad LMS experience.

records.name: Work & Co
records.assessment_markdown:
#### 21. Work & Co

**Relevant niches:** Ecommerce; Real Estate.  
**Project evidence:** IKEA; Lennar.  
**Source records:** E49, E50.

**Why include:** A strong commerce addition because IKEA's case identifies the shopping app, website ecosystem and reusable design work. Lennar's current client-portfolio entry establishes a home-buying experience contribution.

**Limits and questions:** The Real Estate placement is qualified: the current Lennar portfolio entry is much thinner than the IKEA case. Obtain a fuller approved account before detailed claims or a high niche position; do not use a development-preview news draft as proof.
